title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). G is a group, discrete or profinite; the notes fix the profinite case. ρ and σ are elements of G. The previous page sets ε0 = σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = ρσ^{-1}, with ε1 = ρ(ε0) = σ(ε0) where ρ(·) means conjugation. L0 and L1 are the closed procyclic subgroups generated by ε0 and ε1. The bracketed remark there identifies (ρ, σ, ρ^{-1}) with the loops ℓ0, ℓ1, ℓ∞ satisfying ℓ∞ℓ1ℓ0 = 1. So this is an abstract version of the three-punctured-sphere situation, with two 'branch' generators and the 'cusp' subgroup L0, written so that it covers both F̂2 and (P)SL2-type groups.

The map Φ = (ξ, η): Aut(G) → G×G sends u to the pair of commutators ξ = u(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = u(σ)σ^{-1}.

This page:
- (7) defines B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(G) as the automorphisms u such that:
  - u(ρ) is G-conjugate to ρ;
  - u(σ) is G-conjugate to σ;
  - u normalises L0 (equivalently, the notes say, η^{-1}ξ ∈ L1).
- (8) defines Σ_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G×G as the pairs (ξ, η) with:
  - ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}, i.e. ξρ conjugate to ρ;
  - η = βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}, i.e. ησ conjugate to σ;
  - η^{-1}ξ ∈ L1, i.e. ξ = ηε1^ν with ν ∈ Ẑ.
  By construction B = Φ^{-1}(Σ), giving the restriction φ: B → Σ in (9).
- (10) assumes:
  - (a) ρ and σ topologically generate G, so φ is injective;
  - (b) φ is surjective: every (ξ, η) ∈ Σ is realised by an automorphism u_{ξ,η} with u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ, as in (11)–(12).
- One then transports the group structure of B to Σ. The next page gives the law (13): (ξ',η')(ξ,η) = (u_{ξ',η'}(ξ)ξ', u_{ξ',η'}(η)η'). This follows from u'u(ρ) = u'(ξρ) = u'(ξ)ξ'ρ.

This is the same mechanism by which the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group is presented as a set of parameters (λ, f) with a twisted, cocycle-type composition law. Here λ = 1 on ρ and σ, while the 'cusp' generator may be raised to a power: u(ε0) = σ^{-1}η^{-1}ξρ = σ^{-1}(ρσ^{-1})^ν ρ = ε0^{ν+1}.

The next page goes on to build a group G_{ρ,σ} containing G as a normal subgroup, generated by G and an image of B, inducing the given action. The preimage of B under int: G → Aut(G) is computed to be the centraliser N0 of L0. Grothendieck notes that trivial centre is an unreasonable hypothesis, e.g. for SL(2,Ẑ)/±1.

The margin warns 'Attention: this condition is satisfied for G = SL(2,Z)!!'. It apparently refers to condition (b), with some remark about ξ = ε1(μ). So the abstract framework is meant to cover the modular group, i.e. the genus-1, M_{1,1} 'lacets' situation, alongside F̂2.

The problem served is to construct, for a two-generated group with prescribed 'inertia' data, a GT-like group of inertia-preserving automorphisms and the corresponding extension. This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (the GT relations).
errors: The equivalence 'u normalise L0 ⇔ η^{-1}ξ ∈ L1' (previous page) really characterises u(ε0) ∈ L0, namely u(ε0) = ε0^{ν+1}. For u to normalise L0 one needs u(L0) = L0, i.e. ν+1 a unit in Ẑ when L0 ≅ Ẑ. Since Ẑ contains proper closed subgroups isomorphic to itself, this is a small gap (harmless when ε0 is primitive, as in F̂2).
In (8) the exponent ν should lie in Ẑ (profinite context), as on the previous page, not in Z.
The machine transcription writes η = βσβ^{-1}. The intended formula is η = βσ(β)^{-1} = βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}, i.e. ησ conjugate to σ.
The conditions are referred to as '(6)', but on the previous page both blocks are labelled (5); the second should be (6).

Next page: SL(2,Ẑ) is not the profinite completion of SL(2,Z) (no congruence subgroup property). The remark about the centre of SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 is nonetheless correct: the centre is ∏_p{±1}/diagonal, which is nontrivial.

ideas.what: Parametrising inertia-preserving automorphisms of a two-generated (profinite) group by pairs of commutators (ξ, η) = (u(ρ)ρ^{-1}, u(σ)σ^{-1}), with a transported twisted composition law
ideas.modern_name: Parameter description of GT-type groups (pairs (λ, f) with the twisted group law); inertia-preserving / 'braid-like' automorphism groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s) for GT; Lochak–Schneps and others for variants
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action on F̂2 but not this formalism

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatisation: (G, ρ, σ) with cusp subgroups L0, L1 and hypothesis (10b) that every admissible pair is realised by an automorphism; meant to cover both F̂2 and (P)SL2-type groups
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving automorphisms of orbifold fundamental groups of M_{0,4}/M_{1,1}; GT-action on profinite SL2(Z)/B3

ideas.what: Construction of an extension G_{ρ,σ} of B by G when Z(G) ≠ 1, via the centraliser N0 of L0 = int^{-1}(B)
ideas.modern_name: Extension of an outer action by a group with nontrivial centre (crossed-module / 'Galois-type' extension of GT)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that the surjectivity hypothesis (10b), i.e. every admissible pair (ξ, η) comes from an automorphism, holds for SL(2,Z). He intends a uniform formalism treating the genus-0 F̂2 case and the modular-group case on the same footing, with an extension G_{ρ,σ} to be built. The precise verification and the resulting group B for SL2-type groups are not worked out on this page.
missed.quote: Attention cette condition est satisfaite pour G = SL(2,Z) !!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor, but possibly useful, lead for comparing GT-actions on profinite B3 / SL2(Z) completions (genus 1, M_{1,1}) with the genus-0 case inside a single abstract framework. However, comparable results exist in the work of Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and Minamide–Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine set-up of a GT-like automorphism group via commutator parameters with a transported group law. It is well-known in substance (the GT parameter formalism). The only mildly interesting element is the abstract two-generator axiomatisation and the marginal remark about SL(2,Z).
transcription_corrections: In (8): η = βσ(β)^{-1}, i.e. βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}, rather than βσβ^{-1}.
In (8): ν ∈ Ẑ (hat Z), not Z.
'trois conditions (6)' refers to the second (mislabelled (5)) block on the previous page.

Margin: 'Attention cette condition est satisfaite pour G = SL(2,Z) !!' — G is the same gothic/blackboard group as in the text; the rest of the margin is partly illegible ('... ξ = ε1(μ) ... ξ, η ...').
Page heading number at top is 554 (Grothendieck's pagination); archive page 502.
